title.rendered: Best Indian Schools In Dubai 2026: Fees & Ratings

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • 34 Indian Schools Total: Dubai has 34 Indian curriculum schools, the second-largest curriculum group after British schools, serving nearly 100,000 students.
  • KHDA Ratings Frozen: Full school inspections have been paused for 2024-25 and 2025-26, so every current rating comes from the 2023-24 cycle.
  • Two Main Boards: Most follow CBSE, a smaller group follows ICSE (CISCE), and GEMS Modern Academy uniquely runs ICSE alongside IB programmes (PYP, MYP, and DP) on one campus.
  • Fee Range Varies Widely: Annual fees span roughly AED 5,525 at entry grades in affordable schools to AED 73,000 plus at premium Indian curriculum schools.
  • Strong 2025 CBSE Performance: DPS Dubai led the UAE with a 99.4% Class 12 topper, while GEMS Our Own Indian School produced a 99.6% Class 10 topper.

There are 34 Indian curriculum schools across the emirate, fees range from under AED 6,000 to over AED 70,000 a year, and the KHDA ratings you’re reading online are almost certainly from 2023-24 because full inspections have been on pause since. That last bit changes how you should interpret every “Outstanding” and “Very Good” label you see.

This guide cuts through the noise. You’ll get a curated list of the 10 best Indian schools in Dubai for 2026, how CBSE and ICSE differ in practice, and how to plan if your child might switch to IGCSE or IB later. For those transitions, Ignite Training Institute offers IGCSE, A-Level, IB, and AP tutoring in Dubai designed around the real demands of each board.

What Makes Indian Schools In Dubai A Popular Choice?

Indian schools in Dubai follow the CBSE or ICSE curriculum, offer continuity with the Indian education system for families planning a return, and serve the largest expat community in the emirate, with 34 schools teaching nearly 100,000 students. That makes them the second-largest curriculum group in Dubai after British schools, catering to roughly 26 per cent of all private school students despite being under 15 per cent of total schools.

1. Curriculum Continuity For Families Planning A Return To India – Most Indian families in Dubai aren’t here permanently. CBSE is recognised by every Indian university and state board, which means transferring your child back to Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, or Bangalore doesn’t require curriculum re-mapping. ICSE works the same way for families eyeing schools like La Martiniere or Cathedral & John Connon. This is the single biggest reason Indian curriculum schools continue to dominate.

2. Affordability Compared To British Or IB-Only Schools – Indian curriculum schools sit in the most affordable tier of private education in Dubai. A British curriculum school can push AED 80,000 to 120,000 annually at the senior end, whereas Indian schools often land between AED 10,000 and 30,000. You’re not sacrificing academic rigour to save money, you’re just choosing a system with lower overhead and larger cohorts.

3. Cultural Familiarity And Language Support – Most Indian schools in Dubai teach Hindi, Malayalam, or Tamil as second languages alongside Arabic (which is mandatory for all private schools in the UAE). Festivals like Diwali and Onam are marked on the calendar. For younger children, especially, this cultural grounding matters more than parents initially expect.

Know More About: Indian Curriculum Vs British Curriculum: What To Consider? 

The 10 Best Indian Schools In Dubai (2026)

Below is a curated list of ten Indian schools in Dubai that consistently rank at or near the top across KHDA ratings, board exam results, enrolment size, and parent demand. The list covers CBSE, ICSE, and dual-pathway schools, so you can match curriculum to your plans.

1. GEMS Modern Academy

Image Source: Google My Business – www.gemsmodernacademy-dubai.com

Nad Al Sheba (ICSE + IB, Outstanding)

GEMS Modern Academy is the only Indian curriculum school in Dubai holding a KHDA Outstanding rating, and it has held that rating for over a decade. The school runs a dual pathway from Grade 6 onwards: students can continue with the CISCE curriculum leading to ICSE and ISC exams, or switch to the IB Middle Years Programme followed by the IB Diploma in Grades 11 and 12. Fees range roughly from AED 30,000 to AED 74,000 annually, placing it in the mid-premium bracket.

2. Delhi Private School Dubai

Image Source: Google My Business – www.website.dpsdubai.com

Jebel Ali (CBSE, Very Good)

DPS Dubai produced the UAE’s top CBSE Class 12 scorer in 2025 with a 99.4 per cent result and posted a school-wide Class 12 average of 88.6 per cent, reportedly the highest school average in the UAE. The school is large, co-educational, runs KG to Grade 12, and is particularly favoured by families in The Gardens, Al Furjan, and Discovery Gardens. Fees are competitive for the quality delivered, typically sitting in the mid-range for Dubai CBSE schools.

3. The Indian High School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.ihsdubai.org

Oud Metha, Al Garhoud & DSO (CBSE, Very Good)

Founded in 1961, IHS is the oldest Indian expatriate school in Dubai and one of the largest, with roughly 14,000 students across its three campuses. The Oud Metha senior school holds a Very Good rating, while the Al Garhoud junior and DSO campuses are rated Good. Fees are among the most affordable in the emirate, starting around AED 5,525 at KG and rising to just over AED 10,000 at Grade 12. This is a school that trades shine for scale and accessibility.

4. GEMS Our Own Indian School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.gemsoo-alquoz.com

Al Quoz (CBSE, Very Good)

Established in 1991, OIS is a flagship CBSE school in the GEMS network serving around 10,000 students with a KG to Grade 12 programme. In 2025, a Class 10 student from OIS scored 99.6 per cent, joint-highest in the UAE. The school is known for solid academic delivery, disciplined structure, and a merit scholarship programme that awards between 25 and 100 per cent fee concessions to top-performing students.

5. GEMS Our Own English High School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.gemsoo-dubai.com

Al Warqa’a (CBSE, Very Good)

Established in 1968, this is one of Dubai’s oldest girls-focused Indian schools, with over 10,000 students and the CBSE curriculum. It’s co-educational up to Grade 4, then girls-only from Grade 5 through Grade 12. In 2025, its Class 12 topper scored 99 per cent, and the school consistently sends alumni to top-ranked universities globally. Good fit for parents specifically seeking a girls’ school environment for senior years.

6. Ambassador School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.ambassadorschool.com

Bur Dubai (ICSE, Very Good)

Founded in 2010, Ambassador is one of the most credible ICSE options in Dubai, rated Very Good by KHDA. It runs pre-KG to Grade 12, following the CISCE curriculum with an emphasis on inquiry-based learning and practical experience. The school has won a Golden Peacock Award for excellence in innovation. Fees are in the low-to-mid range for ICSE schools, which makes it a strong value pick for families committed to the ICSE board.

7. JSS International School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.jssisdubai.com

JVC (ICSE, Very Good)

JSS follows the ICSE curriculum from pre-KG to Grade 12 and has held its Very Good rating since 2019. With around 2,500 students and a teacher-to-student ratio of roughly 1:11 (one of the lowest among Indian schools), it leans into individualised attention. It also offers door-to-door transport across Dubai and Sharjah, which matters more than it sounds when you’re working against Dubai traffic.

8. GEMS New Millennium School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.gemsnewmillenniumschool-alkhail.com

Al Khail (CBSE + IGCSE/A-Level, Very Good)

This is a dual-curriculum CBSE plus British pathway school. Students follow CBSE from pre-KG through Grade 8, then at Grade 9 choose between continuing CBSE to Grade 12 or switching to IGCSE, AS Level, and A Level. That flexibility is rare in Indian schools and valuable if your child is aiming at UK or international universities. The school is rated Very Good and sits conveniently off Al Khail Road near Dubai Hills.

9. The Millennium School

Image Source: Google My Business – www.themillenniumschool-dubai.com

Al Qusais (CBSE, Very Good)

Established in 2000, TMS is a CBSE school rated Very Good, serving KG to Grade 12 with a broad extracurricular programme covering MUN, debates, academy exchanges, and sports. It’s well-positioned for families in Al Qusais, Mirdif, and Al Rashidiya. Fees sit in the mid-range for Dubai CBSE schools. The school has built a reputation for balanced academic and co-curricular outcomes rather than a narrow focus.

10. Amity School Dubai

Image Source: Google My Business – www.amityschooldubai.com

Al Qusais (CBSE, Outstanding)

Amity School is a newer entrant (established in 2017) but earned an Outstanding KHDA rating in the 2023-24 cycle, an unusual feat for a school so young. It runs a 14-acre campus, follows CBSE from pre-KG to Grade 9 and 11, and integrates UAE Ministry of Education requirements. Worth shortlisting if you’re in the Al Qusais or Sharjah corridor and want a modern campus with an aggressive academic trajectory.

Indian Schools In Dubai With Fees 

Fees at Indian schools in Dubai are probably the single biggest reason they remain the most popular choice among expat families. 

Entry-Grade Fees (KG To Grade 4)

At the lowest end, schools like The Indian High School start around AED 5,525 at KG level. Mid-range CBSE schools sit between AED 9,000 and 15,000 at primary level. ICSE schools tend to start higher, typically AED 12,000 to 18,000. GEMS Modern Academy, at the premium end, starts around AED 30,000 at pre-KG.

Senior-Grade Fees (Grade 9 To Grade 12)

Senior fees climb substantially. Affordable CBSE schools cost around AED 10,000 to 15,000 at Grade 12. Mid-range schools land between AED 18,000 and 30,000. Premium schools, especially those offering dual IB or A-Level pathways, can push past AED 50,000 in senior years. This is where the board choice starts affecting your budget significantly.

Fees are indicative and based on the most recently published data. Confirm the current academic year fee with each school directly.

Know More About: Difference between IGCSE and CBSE for senior-year students 

CBSE vs ICSE In Dubai: Which Board Should You Choose?

Both boards are strong. The right choice depends less on which is “better” and more on where your child is headed academically and geographically.

What CBSE Offers?

CBSE is the default choice for most Indian families in Dubai. It’s streamlined, exam-focused, and specifically aligned with competitive Indian entrance exams like JEE (engineering) and NEET (medical). The syllabus is issued by the Central Board of Secondary Education, New Delhi, and the same textbooks are used globally. If your child might sit JEE, NEET, or apply to Indian universities, CBSE is the path of least friction.

What ICSE / CISCE Offers?

ICSE, run by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations, tends to be more rigorous in English and the humanities. It goes broader in its subject range, particularly at Grade 10 (ICSE) and Grade 12 (ISC). It’s also more commonly associated with students who plan to apply to international universities or pursue liberal arts degrees. ICSE’s English standard in particular is noticeably stronger than CBSE’s.

Which Schools Offer An IB Or IGCSE Pathway Alongside CBSE Or ICSE?

This is the often-overlooked criterion. GEMS Modern Academy lets students switch from ICSE to the IB Diploma in Grades 11-12. GEMS New Millennium lets CBSE students move to IGCSE at Grade 9 and A-Levels thereafter. If you’re undecided about university destinations (India vs UK vs US), these dual-pathway schools give you optionality without forcing an early commitment. That’s valuable because the decision to switch often comes at Grade 8 or 9, when students are still figuring out what they enjoy.

Know More About: CBSE or IB Board: comparative analysis and popular facts 

2025 CBSE Results: Which Dubai Indian Schools Performed Best?

The May 2025 CBSE results gave a clear snapshot of academic output across Dubai’s Indian schools. Gulf News reported that 13,520 UAE students sat Grade 10 and 9,829 sat Grade 12, with several schools posting remarkable outcomes.

DPS Dubai Leads UAE With 88.6% Class 12 Average

Delhi Private School Dubai posted the highest school-wide Class 12 average in the UAE at 88.6 per cent, with a 95 per cent distinction rate. DPS also hit a Class 10 average of 89.7 per cent with 123 students scoring a perfect 100 per cent in at least one subject.

GEMS Schools Dominated Individual Toppers

GEMS Our Own Indian School produced the UAE’s joint Grade 10 topper at 99.6 per cent. The class 12 science topper scored 99 per cent. Across the GEMS Indian curriculum network, 3,131 Grade 10 and 2,266 Grade 12 students appeared for CBSE exams, with strong distinction rates across the board.

Ignite: IGCSE, A-Level, IB, & AP Tutoring In Dubai For Indian School Students

Here’s the transition point most Indian families hit. A child starts in a CBSE or ICSE school, does well through primary and middle school, and then, around Grade 8 or 9, the question of university destination starts shaping decisions. 

If the answer is the UK, US, or international universities, the conversation often shifts to IGCSE, A-Level, IB, or AP pathways. Schools like GEMS Modern Academy and GEMS New Millennium make this in-house, but the academic shift from Indian boards to international ones is non-trivial.

That’s where structured external tutoring helps. Ignite Training Institute specialises in expert IGCSE tutors in Dubai, IB tutors in Dubai, and A-Level tutors in Dubai, focused on the real difficulty points in each pathway. Past paper drills, concept-by-concept gap fixing, and personalised planning are the core of how the programme works.

One parent shared that her daughter, after studying with Ignite across IGCSE and IB over three years, secured offers from University College London and the University of Edinburgh. That kind of outcome is typical of students who start the international curriculum transition with structured support rather than figuring it out as they go. 

Know More About: 10 proven strategies on how to study for IGCSE exams and excel 

FAQs

1. How Many Indian Schools Are There In Dubai?

Dubai has 34 Indian curriculum schools, making Indian schools the second-largest curriculum group after British schools. Across these 34 schools, roughly 99,603 students are enrolled, which works out to around 26 per cent of all private school students in the emirate. Most follow CBSE, a smaller group follows ICSE (CISCE), and a couple run dual pathways with IB or IGCSE.

2. Which Is The Highest-Rated Indian School In Dubai?

GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba is the only Indian curriculum school currently holding a KHDA Outstanding rating, and has held that rating since 2011. Amity School in Al Qusais also achieved an Outstanding rating in the 2023-24 cycle, which was notable given the school was only established in 2017. 

3. Are Indian Schools In Dubai Affordable?

Compared to British or IB-only schools, yes. Fees at Indian schools in Dubai typically range from around AED 5,525 at entry grades in the most affordable schools to AED 70,000 plus at premium dual-curriculum schools. For context, British schools often land between AED 45,000 and AED 80,000 annually at senior grades, and premium IB schools can exceed AED 120,000. Most Indian CBSE schools fall in the AED 10,000 to AED 30,000 range for most grades.

4. Can My Child Transfer From A CBSE School In Dubai To India?

Yes, and this is one of the main reasons families choose CBSE in the first place. Since all CBSE schools use the same NCERT textbooks and syllabus worldwide, a student moving from DPS Dubai to DPS Delhi faces minimal curriculum disruption. The same applies to ICSE students transferring to CISCE-affiliated schools in India. Just ensure you have the school leaving certificate, transfer certificate, and academic records attested.

5. Do Indian Schools In Dubai Offer IB Or IGCSE Alongside CBSE?

A small but important number do. GEMS Modern Academy offers a dual pathway with the Indian CISCE curriculum (leading to ICSE and ISC exams) alongside the IB Diploma Programme in Grades 11-12, with IB PYP in primary years. 

GEMS New Millennium offers CBSE plus IGCSE from Grade 9 and A-Levels thereafter. These dual-pathway schools give families flexibility without forcing a mid-school switch. Students transitioning between streams often use personalised tutoring support to bridge the curriculum gap.

6. When Do Admissions Open For Indian Schools In Dubai?

Most Indian schools start admission cycles in November for the April academic year start. Top schools like DPS Dubai and GEMS Our Own Indian School fill seats fast at entry points (KG and Grade 1), so applying six to twelve months ahead is sensible. Apply to two or three schools in parallel rather than waiting for a single decision. 

7. What Languages Do Indian Schools In Dubai Teach Besides English?

Hindi is offered as a core or elective language at most Indian schools, and Arabic is mandatory across all private schools in the UAE. Several schools teach regional Indian languages, with Malayalam common at Kerala-origin schools and Tamil available at JSS International. French and Spanish appear as foreign language electives at some ICSE schools.

5. What Documents Are Needed For Admission To An Indian School In Dubai?

You will need the child’s passport with a valid UAE residence visa, Emirates ID, birth certificate, immunisation record, and the last two years of report cards, plus a transfer certificate from the previous school. Parents submit passport copies, visa copies, and Emirates ID. Documents from overseas schools need the ministry and UAE embassy attestation, so plan for two to three weeks.

Conclusion

Choosing from the best Indian schools in Dubai gets easier once you filter for three things: curriculum fit for your likely university destination, KHDA rating (treated as a 2023-24 snapshot rather than a live signal), and practical fit in terms of fees and commute. 

If your child is heading toward IGCSE, A-Level, IB, or AP in the senior years, external tutoring support during the transition is often the difference between a smooth shift and a stressful one. Book a free demo class with Ignite Training Institute to see how structured board-specific tutoring works before you commit.
